key_insight: A model-agnostic “cannot-miss” prompt can substantially reduce missed escalations for subtle emergencies, especially when the danger is atypical rather than merely downplayed.
clinical_relevance: For patient-message triage, the key safety risk is failing to escalate time-critical conditions, so deterministic escalation rules may improve consistency without harming detection of obvious emergencies.
method: Prompt-level ablation on Claude Opus 4.8 across five framings of 40 unambiguous emergencies.
Replicated the same instruction across eight models from Claude and Gemini families under a documented harness.
Evaluated 76 subtle or atypical emergencies with blinded, LLM-simulated three-physician adjudication and guideline-linked cannot-miss diagnoses.
evidence_signal: In subtle emergencies, failure to escalate to top acuity fell from 13.2% to 3.9% with the governance prompt, while overt emergencies stayed at 97.5% to 100% sensitivity across framings.
watch_item: These results depend on a specific evaluation harness and LLM-based adjudication, so real-world performance and generalization to other settings still need prospective validation.
paper_title: Reasoning Before Disposition: A Model-Agnostic Cannot-Miss Discipline for Quiet Emergencies and the Case for Deterministic Enforcement
